diagnosis.summary: Your passion fruit plants in Lugari are suffering from rotting stems, which threatens to kill the vines.
likely_causes: A soil-borne fungus called Fusarium wilt which attacks the base of passion fruit vines.
Collar rot disease which thrives in wet, poorly drained soils.
Injuries from weeding tools that allow rot-causing germs to enter the stem.
diagnosis.recommended_approach: Improve soil drainage to prevent soggy conditions, and apply wood ash to the affected stem bases to dry out the rot.

this_week_actions: Carefully scrape away weeds and soil touching the base of the infected passion fruit stems to let them breathe.
Dig shallow drainage trenches around the garden block to direct standing rainwater away from the root zones.
Apply a handful of dry wood ash directly onto the rotting parts of the stems to dry out the infections.
Disinfect all weeding and pruning tools with a bleach solution after working on each plant to stop disease spread.
materials_needed: Dry wood ash collected from your kitchen fireplace.
A hand hoe or shovel to dig the drainage trenches.
Household bleach mixed with water in a container to clean your tools.
warning_signs: The leaves on the passion fruit vines suddenly wilt and turn yellow despite the soil being wet.
The black or brown rot completely wraps around the stem, causing the bark to peel away entirely.
action_plan.expected_outcome: You should see the wet, mushy rot on the stems dry up and vine wilting stop within two weeks.
